Required fields:

Optional fields:

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

## Mathmatical Model

A complete mathematical model is as follows,
### Variables
$$
\begin{aligned}
& S^g_k \quad \forall k\in G  \text{ : generator complex power dispatch} \\
& V_i \quad \forall i\in N  \text{ : bus complex voltage} \\
& S_{ij} \quad \forall (i,j) \in E \cup E^R \text{ : branch complex power flow} \\
\\
\end{aligned}
$$

### Formulation
$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{minimize:} &
\sum_{k \in G} c_{2k} (\Re(S^g_k))^2 + c_{1k}\Re(S^g_k) + c_{0k} \\

\text{subject to:} & \\
& \angle V_{r} = 0 \quad \forall r \in R \\
& S^{gl}_k \leq S^g_k \leq S^{gu}_k \quad \forall k \in G \\
& v^l_i \leq |V_i| \leq v^u_i \quad \forall i \in N \\
& \sum_{k \in G_i} S^g_k - \sum_{k \in L_i} S^d_k - \sum_{k \in S_i} (Y^s_k)^* |V_i|^2 = \sum_{(i,j)\in E_i \cup E_i^R} S_{ij} \quad \forall i\in N \\
& S_{ij} = (Y_{ij} + Y^c_{ij})^* \frac{|V_i|^2}{|T_{ij}|^2} - Y^*_{ij} \frac{V_i V^*_j}{T_{ij}} \quad \forall (i,j)\in E \\
& S_{ji} = (Y_{ij} + Y^c_{ji})^* |V_j|^2 - Y^*_{ij} \frac{V^*_i V_j}{T^*_{ij}} \quad \forall (i,j)\in E \\
& |S_{ij}| \leq s^u_{ij} \quad \forall (i,j) \in E \cup E^R \\
& |S_{ij}| \leq |V_i| i^u_{ij} \quad \forall (i,j) \in E \cup E^R \\
& \theta^{\Delta l}_{ij} \leq \angle (V_i V^*_j) \leq \theta^{\Delta u}_{ij} \quad \forall (i,j) \in E
\end{aligned}
$$

import json
import numpy as np
from pyomo.environ import *
from pyomo.opt import SolverFactory

# Load network data
with open('network.json', 'r') as f:
    network_data = json.load(f)

base_mva = network_data['baseMVA']

# Parse bus data
bus_data = {}
for bus in network_data['bus']:
    bus_id = int(bus[0])
    bus_data[bus_id] = {
        'type': int(bus[1]),  # 1=PQ, 2=PV, 3=Slack
        'pd': bus[2],  # MW
        'qd': bus[3],  # MVAr
        'gs': bus[4],  # shunt conductance
        'bs': bus[5],  # shunt susceptance
        'vm': bus[7],  # voltage magnitude
        'va': bus[8],  # voltage angle
        'vmax': bus[11],  # max voltage
        'vmin': bus[12],  # min voltage
    }

# Parse generator data
gen_data = {}
for i, gen in enumerate(network_data['gen']):
    gen_id = i + 1
    gen_data[gen_id] = {
        'bus': int(gen[0]),
        'pg': gen[1],  # MW
        'qg': gen[2],  # MVAr
        'qmax': gen[3],  # MVAr
        'qmin': gen[4],  # MVAr
        'vg': gen[5],  # voltage setpoint
        'pmax': gen[8],  # MW
        'pmin': gen[9],  # MW
        'status': int(gen[7]),  # 1=in-service
    }

# Parse branch data
branch_data = {}
for i, branch in enumerate(network_data['branch']):
    branch_id = i + 1
    branch_data[branch_id] = {
        'fbus': int(branch[0]),
        'tbus': int(branch[1]),
        'r': branch[2],  # pu
        'x': branch[3],  # pu
        'b': branch[4],  # pu
        'rate_a': branch[5],  # MVA
        'tap': branch[8],  # transformer tap
        'shift': branch[9],  # phase shift degrees
        'status': int(branch[10]),  # 1=in-service
        'angmin': branch[11],  # degrees
        'angmax': branch[12],  # degrees
    }

# Parse generator cost data
gen_cost = {}
for i, cost in enumerate(network_data['gencost']):
    gen_id = i + 1
    if int(cost[0]) == 2:  # polynomial
        ncost = int(cost[3])
        coeffs = cost[4:4+ncost]
        gen_cost[gen_id] = coeffs
    else:
        gen_cost[gen_id] = [0, 0, 0]  # default

print(f'Loaded network with {len(bus_data)} buses, {len(gen_data)} generators, {len(branch_data)} branches')
print(f'Generator cost example (gen 1): {gen_cost[1]}')

EOPYTHON
